doc:
A category with a zero object has zero morphisms.

It is rarely a good idea to use this. Many categories that have a zero object have zero
morphisms for some other reason, for example from additivity. Library code that uses
`zeroMorphismsOfZeroObject` will then be incompatible with these categories because
the `HasZeroMorphisms` instances will not be definitionally equal. For this reason library
code should generally ask for an instance of `HasZeroMorphisms` separately, even if it already
asks for an instance of `HasZeroObject`.

fun {C} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {J}
    [CategoryTheory.Category.{w', w} J] {K₁ K₂} F h [CategoryTheory.CreatesLimit K₁ F] =>
  have __src := ⋯;
  { toReflectsLimit := __src,
    lifts := fun c t =>
      have t' :=
        (CategoryTheory.Limits.IsLimit.postcomposeInvEquiv
              (CategoryTheory.Functor.isoWhiskerRight h F) c).symm
          t;
      {
        liftedCone :=
          (CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.postcompose h.hom).obj (CategoryTheory.liftLimit t'),
        validLift :=
          F.mapConePostcompose ≪≫
            (CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.postcompose
                    (CategoryTheory.Functor.isoWhiskerRight h F).hom).mapIso
                (CategoryTheory.liftedLimitMapsToOriginal t') ≪≫
              CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.ext
                (CategoryTheory.Iso.refl
                  ((CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.postcompose
                          (CategoryTheory.Functor.isoWhiskerRight h F).hom).obj
                      ((CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.postcompose
                            (CategoryTheory.Functor.isoWhiskerRight h F).inv).obj
                        c)).pt)
                ⋯ } }

A helper to show a functor creates limits. In particular, if we can show
that for any limit cone `c` for `K ⋙ F`, there is a lift of it which is
a limit and `F` reflects isomorphisms, then `F` creates limits.
Usually, `F` creating limits says that _any_ lift of `c` is a limit, but
here we only need to show that our particular lift of `c` is a limit.

doc:
If `F` reflects isomorphisms and we can lift a single limit cone to a limit cone, then `F`
creates limits. Note that unlike `createsLimitOfReflectsIso`, to apply this result it is
necessary to know that `K ⋙ F` actually has a limit.
If `F` creates limits of shape `J` and `J ≌ J'`, then `F` creates limits of shape `J'`.

value.text:
fun {C} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v₁, u₁} C] {D} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v₂, u₂} D] {J}
    [CategoryTheory.Category.{w', w} J] {J'} [CategoryTheory.Category.{w'₁, w₁} J'] e F
    [CategoryTheory.CreatesLimitsOfShape J F] =>
  {
    CreatesLimit := fun {K} =>
      have __ReflectsLimit := ⋯;
      { toReflectsLimit := __ReflectsLimit,
        lifts := fun c hc =>
          {
            liftedCone :=
              (CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.whiskeringEquivalence e).inverse.obj
                (CategoryTheory.liftLimit (hc.whiskerEquivalence e)),
            validLift :=
              CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.ext
                  (CategoryTheory.Iso.refl
                    (F.mapCone
                        ((CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.whiskeringEquivalence e).inverse.obj
                          (CategoryTheory.liftLimit (hc.whiskerEquivalence e)))).pt)
                  ⋯ ≪≫
                (CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.whiskeringEquivalence e).inverse.mapIso
                    (CategoryTheory.liftedLimitMapsToOriginal (hc.whiskerEquivalence e)) ≪≫
                  ((CategoryTheory.Limits.Cone.whiskeringEquivalence e).unitIso.app c).symm } } }
